dimensions.assessment: Affects motor carriers, brokers, freight forwarders, state enforcement agencies, and consumers shipping household goods interstate.
dimensions.evidence: motor carriers, brokers, and freight forwarders to designate a principal place of business

dimensions.assessment: Enhances federal and state enforcement, allows administrative civil penalties, enables registration revocation for lack of a principal place of business, and lets states retain collected fines.
dimensions.evidence: withhold, suspend, amend, or revoke any part of a registration... if the Secretary finds that the motor carrier... failed to designate a valid principal place of business

dimensions.assessment: Allows states to use existing grant funds (MCSAP and High Priority) for enforcement and retain collected fines, without specifying new federal appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: any fine or penalty imposed on a carrier or broker in a proceeding under this section shall be paid to, and retained by, the State

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 49 of the United States Code to alter registration requirements, grant fund uses, state fine retentions, and administrative penalty enforcement authorities.
dimensions.evidence: The Act may be cited as the 'Household Goods Shipping Consumer Protection Act'.

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent statutory changes to federal transportation laws and regulatory oversight mechanisms.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 49, United States Code, to clarify the authority of the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

missing_information: Total amount of grant funds states are expected to reallocate toward this enforcement.
Exact volume of interstate household goods movers operating without a designated principal place of business.
importance_detail.rationale: Expands Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration authority to assess civil penalties for household goods shipping violations, mandates principal place of business designations, requires relationship disclosures, and permits states to use certain grant funds for enforcement.
